title: v5.12.1 — Proper app name on Android
items: The Android app is now called "Concorde EFB" under its icon and in the app list, instead of the internal name

title: v5.12.0 — Smarter gear-up warning
items: The gear-up warning no longer fires on every descent. Within 30 nm of the destination, below 5,000 ft above the airport and under 250 kt with the gear up you get a single amber GEAR UP — CHECK GEAR reminder; only within 10 nm, below 2,000 ft and under 220 kt does it become the repeating red GEAR UP — TOO LOW warning
Both gear alerts can be cleared with a tap (e.g. for a hold or low-level procedure); they re-arm once the gear goes down or you climb away

title: v5.11.0 — Clearable DESCEND NOW
items: Tap DESCEND NOW on the Flight Monitor to clear it (no pill, no chime) when ATC, the procedure or terrain keep you level. It re-arms automatically once you leave cruise or start a new flight. Other warnings still silence for 10 seconds on tap

title: v5.10.1 — Removed the force supersonic switch
items: Removed the FORCE SUPERSONIC switch; short sectors are planned subsonic again (the cruise speed on the dispatch strip stays)

title: v5.10.0 — Force supersonic switch, cruise speed on the dispatch strip
items: New FORCE SUPERSONIC switch under the cruise level: fly Mach 2 even on sectors too short for it to pay off (as long as the climb, acceleration and descent fit). The cruise level, fuel and times follow, showing the real, higher fuel cost
The dispatch strip now shows the cruise speed at the planned level (e.g. CRZ M2.04 · 1170 KT, or M0.95 when subsonic), and fits on one line

title: v5.9.1 — One-line dispatch strip
items: A clean DISPATCH GO is now a single strip: the V-speeds, weights, fuel, level and runways sit right next to it instead of an 'all checks passed' line

title: v5.9.0 — Quick-glance dispatch figures
items: When dispatch is GO, the dispatch strip now shows V1 / VR / V2, takeoff weight, fuel, cruise level, departure runway, landing weight, VAPP and arrival runway at a glance
Removed the 'runway narrower than 150 ft' caution from the dispatch strip (still shown on the performance cards)
Clearing the cruise flight level box to type a new level no longer snaps it back to FL590
Flight progress bar stays at the start while taxiing and starts moving once airborne

title: v5.8.3 — Flight progress starts at the gate
items: Distance to destination and the progress bar now match the planned route distance, so the aircraft no longer looks well en route while still parked at the gate

title: v5.8.2 — Smart cruise level for typed distances and .pln imports
items: The automatic cruise level now also applies when you type a planned distance or import an MSFS .pln file: supersonic as high as the distance allows, otherwise the .pln's level when it fits (raised to around FL290 if lower), or the suggested subsonic level for a typed distance. You can still change it by hand

title: v5.8.1 — Smarter cruise level on short sectors
items: On sectors too short for supersonic, SimBrief's level is kept when it fits; if it's lower than ideal for Concorde, the app raises it to around FL290 (FL280 westbound) when the distance allows, and lowers it if it doesn't fit

title: v5.8.0 — Smart cruise level from SimBrief, clearer fuel endurance
items: Loading a SimBrief flight now picks the cruise level for you: if the route is long enough to go supersonic, the highest Mach 2 level the distance allows (up to FL590); on short sectors, SimBrief's own planned level. Fuel and times follow automatically, and you can still change the level by hand
ENDURANCE MARGIN is now FUEL ENDURANCE: how long the fuel on board lasts, with the flight time + reserves it covers and any extra margin

title: v5.7.0 — Takeoff CG target
items: The CG card now shows a 56% TAKEOFF TARGET on the ground and below 10,000 ft, with transfer advice towards it; above 10,000 ft it switches to the Mach-based target and limits

title: v5.6.1 — Attitude indicator and climb alert fixes
items: The Flight Monitor attitude indicator now banks the right way (it was mirrored)
CG AFT / FWD LIMIT warnings only arm above 10,000 ft, so takeoff and initial climb with the takeoff CG stay quiet
No more false FUEL BELOW FINAL RESERVE during takeoff and climb: fuel at destination now uses the planned cruise burn until you're actually cruising, and fuel warnings arm from cruise onwards

title: v5.6.0 — No alarms in the MSFS menu, tap to silence
items: No alerts or chimes while MSFS is in its menu or loading screen — the Flight Monitor waits until a flight is actually loaded (no more 8,000 NM to destination or negative fuel)
CG AFT / FWD LIMIT warnings only arm once all four engines are running (or in flight), so fuelling and trim transfers at the gate stay quiet
Tap a warning on the MFD strip to silence its chime for 10 seconds; if the problem is still there afterwards it chimes again
Chimes and silencing are per device: muting on the PC doesn't mute the phone or tablet, and vice versa

title: v5.5.9 — Smaller, roomier layout on phones
items: On phones the whole app is now drawn about 15% smaller, so more fits on screen and nothing feels oversized
The Settings window now scrolls on short phone screens instead of running off the bottom

title: v5.5.8 — Android ads use the app's own ad account
items: The Android app now shows its bottom banner from the app's own ad account, which helps fund development. Test builds still show harmless sample ads

title: v5.5.7 — Better-fitting Android ad banner
items: The Android ad banner now sizes itself to your screen width instead of a fixed small banner

title: v5.5.6 — New Android app identity
items: The Android app now uses its permanent package name (com.theawesomeray.concorde_efb). If you installed an earlier Android test build, uninstall it first; this installs as a separate app

title: v5.5.5 — Android ad setup
items: Android release builds are now prepared to use the app's own ad configuration; test builds always show harmless sample ads

title: v5.5.4 — Airport data cache works when installed in Program Files
items: On Windows the airport database cache is now stored in your user profile, so it saves reliably instead of re-downloading on every launch

title: v5.5.3 — Cleaner Windows installs and updates
items: Updating Concorde EFB now fully replaces the previous version's files, so leftovers from old versions can no longer cause problems
Uninstalling now removes the whole install folder; your settings are kept for the next install

title: v5.5.2 — Version number now always matches the build
items: The version shown in Settings and the update check now come from the app's real build version instead of a stale hardcoded value
The Windows installer now reports the correct version in Add/Remove Programs

title: v5.5.1 — Altitude fixes for high-elevation airports
items: GEAR UP — BELOW 250 KT now triggers below 5,000 ft above the arrival airport (was 5,000 ft above sea level, which never fired at airports like Denver or Mexico City)
Top of descent and ETA now account for the destination airport's elevation
Flight Monitor no longer reads a parked aircraft at a high airport as airborne

title: v5.5.0 — Repeating chimes for urgent warnings
items: Urgent warnings (Mach overspeed, gear overspeed, CG limits, gear up below 250 kt on approach) now re-chime every 2 seconds until corrected
DESCEND NOW re-chimes every 12 seconds until you start down
Other alerts still chime once
Warning chime is louder (same sound)

title: v5.4.0 — Alert chimes
items: Flight Monitor alerts now chime once when they appear: a two-tone chime for red warnings, a single soft chime for amber cautions — never a repeating master-caution loop
Alerts are checked on every tab, so you hear them even while on the Planner or Checklists
Mute with the speaker button on the alert row, or in Settings → Alert chimes (with test buttons for each chime)

title: v5.3.0 — Numbers from the DC Designs Concorde manual
items: CG limits and ideal CG now follow the manual's CG-vs-Mach chart (about 53.5–54% MAC for takeoff and landing, 59% at Mach 2); the Flight Monitor's TRANSFER AFT / FWD advice uses it
Takeoff speeds at MTOW match the manual: V1 170 / VR 190 kt, lift-off ~210–220 kt
Approach speeds match the manual's 150–207 kt range by weight (VREF 195 kt at max landing weight)
Takeoff runway required at MTOW (sea level, ISA, no wind) is now the manual's 2,743 m
Fuel plan: reheat acceleration now starts at FL240 / Mach 0.95 as in the manual
Flight Monitor: GEAR UP — BELOW 250 KT warning on approach (the manual's gear-light warning)
Dispatch: ramp weight checked against the 187,000 kg max taxi weight
Checklists: reheat and fuel-transfer steps now give the manual's exact speeds, levels and tank settings

title: v5.2.0 — Flight Monitor redesign
items: New glass-cockpit Flight Monitor: primary flight display with an artificial horizon (pitch ladder, roll scale) between speed/Mach and altitude/vertical-speed readouts, plus heading, gear, nose and G
Route progress bar: departure to arrival with your aircraft's position and the top-of-descent marker
Engine panel: four throttle bars with per-engine reheat lights and total fuel flow
CG & trim: the allowed CG range for your current Mach with a target marker, TRANSFER AFT / FWD / ON TARGET advice and forward/aft trim tank contents
Fuel schematic legend no longer overflows on tablets

title: v5.1.0 — Flight Monitor on phones & tablets over Wi-Fi
items: Desktop: new SHARE TO PHONE / TABLET switch on the Flight Monitor tab shows this PC's address and a 6-digit pairing code

Phone/tablet: the Flight Monitor finds your sim PC on the same Wi-Fi automatically (or enter its address), pair once with the code, and get the full live Monitor — MFD strip, fuel schematic, CG, engines — plus checklists that follow your flight phase
Sharing is off by default, local-network only and protected by the pairing code; NEW CODE un-pairs every device
Privacy policy updated to describe Wi-Fi sharing (data stays on your own network)

title: v5.0.0 — Cleaner cockpit layout
items: Top status bar fits on one row on desktops and tablets: compact pills for call sign, registration, pax, route and ETE / climb / cruise / descent times; the sim status now lives only on the navigation rail dot
Fuel release stamp now reads OVER CAPACITY when the plan asks for more fuel than the tanks hold (it used to say FUEL SHORT)
Weight and endurance details under the fuel stats no longer get cut off
Route chip shows just the route — distance and time are in the top bar
Footer simplified to the support card only (changelog, Discord and support links are in Settings)

title: v4.5.0 — Status bar flight times & solid dispatch banner
items: Top status bar: call sign, registration and pax are always shown, plus planned TOTAL, CLIMB, CRUISE and DESCENT times
Dispatch banner moved above the Planner / Performance selector and redesigned as a solid, bold status block (green GO, amber CAUTION, red NO-GO)
Privacy Policy (and Ad Privacy Options where required) moved into the Settings menu
Removed the Design Lab entry from the Settings menu

title: v4.4.0 — Phone layout, smarter runways & Flight Monitor redesign
items: Runways: the default runway is now the longest one without a tailwind (avoiding strong crosswinds) and follows METAR updates until you pick one yourself — no more false NO-GO from a tailwind runway
Wind arrows are coloured by what the wind does to that runway: green comfortable, amber close to limits or any tailwind, red outside limits
Phones: status bar scrolls away, compact navigation rail, one-line dispatch banner (tap to expand), fuel release strip stacks under the inputs, no overflowing layouts
Checklists: on phones, phases are a horizontal strip; with the sim connected, the current flight phase is selected automatically and other phases are greyed out
Planner: Flight Plan card condensed into one row with the route, distance and ETE together
Planner: fuel card shows a single ENDURANCE MARGIN instead of two identical times
Flight Monitor: one compact flight-data bar (IAS, Mach, TAS, GS, ALT, V/S, HDG, attitude, gear, nose) so the fuel schematic, CG and engines sit above the fold
Status bar: call sign / registration / pax only appear once a flight is loaded
Fixed gusty winds overlapping in the METAR strip

title: v4.3.0 — Route distances everywhere
items: Fuel and time are planned on the distance actually flown along the route (SID, airways, STAR), not the straight line between airports
Imported .pln plans: distance is now the sum of every route leg, using each fix's coordinates
SimBrief: the route's fixes and the alternate's planned route distance are imported
Flight Monitor: distance to destination, top of descent, ETA and fuel at destination now follow your route's remaining legs
Alternate fuel uses the planned alternate route distance when SimBrief provides it

title: v4.2.0 — Privacy policy & ad consent
items: New privacy policy page, linked from the app footer (PRIVACY)
Android: Google's consent form is shown to users in the EEA, UK and Switzerland before ads load; AD PRIVACY OPTIONS in the footer lets you change your choice at any time
Android: ads now only load after the consent check; desktop remains ad-free

title: v4.1.0 — Dispatch banner & Flight Monitor MFD
items: Planner: new DISPATCH banner (GO / GO · CAUTION / NO-GO) listing every fuel, weight, runway, wind and alternate issue in one place
Planner: raw METAR is always shown (selectable) under the weather strip — no more tap to reveal

Flight Monitor: new MFD strip with flight phase, distance to destination, top of descent, ETA, predicted fuel at destination vs reserves, and warning annunciators (CG limit, MMO, gear speed, low fuel at destination, descend now)
Flight Monitor: fixed gear always showing TRANSIT when down, and droop/visor showing 0°/1° — now shows UP / 5° / 12.5°
Flight Monitor: CG limits now follow Mach (the corridor moves aft going supersonic) instead of a fixed 52–59 % band
Flight Monitor: estimated airtime uses the sim's actual (smoothed) fuel flow; burn-rate readout no longer flickers
Flight Monitor: last touchdown stays on screen (with time) instead of disappearing after 5 seconds

title: v4.0.0 — Planner polish
items: Fuel release strip header now shows your actual flight: call sign / route, plan source, cruise FL, distance and ETE, with a FUEL OK / FUEL SHORT stamp
Performance METAR strip reorganised into two clean rows: flight category + conditions, then equal-width WIND / VIS / TEMP / QNH / ELEV readouts
METAR age moved below the strip and spelled out (e.g. OBSERVED 36 MINS AGO), flagged OUTDATED after 90 minutes

title: Rebuilt SimConnect bridge
items: Flight Monitor: SimConnect bridge rewritten from scratch for reliable, always-on connection to MSFS 2020/2024
Connects automatically whenever MSFS starts, and reconnects by itself after the sim quits, crashes or reloads
Bridge no longer opens a console window, restarts itself if it ever crashes, and clears hung bridges left from older versions
Status bar now explains exactly what it's waiting for (MSFS not running, in menu/paused, etc.)
Fixed ground speed being shown in m/s instead of knots

title: v3.7.0 — Fuel & performance model overhaul
items: Fuel: rebuilt the trip-fuel model phase by phase (takeoff, subsonic climb, transonic acceleration, Mach 2 cruise-climb, descent) and calibrated it against real Concorde sectors (LHR–JFK ≈ 71 t trip, 3h13 airborne)
Fuel: short sectors are automatically planned subsonic and at a lower level, instead of always climbing to Mach 2
Fuel: alternate fuel now uses a proper subsonic diversion profile, and you get a warning when no alternate is set, it's the arrival airport, or it's more than 500 nm away
Fuel: endurance check now uses the fuel that actually fits in the tanks, with reserves burned at holding fuel flow
Weights: takeoff weight no longer includes taxi fuel; ZFW and landing weight are shown
Performance: 10 kt tailwind limit, gusts now count toward crosswind/tailwind limits, and variable winds are treated as worst case
Performance: a missing METAR is flagged instead of being treated as calm wind
Performance: new runway condition selector (AUTO/DRY/WET/CONTAM) — AUTO reads rain/snow/freezing precipitation from the METAR
Performance: takeoff distance scales with weight squared; V-speeds recalibrated (V1 165 / VR 195 / V2 220 kt at MTOW, VREF 165 kt at MLW) with wet/contaminated V1 reduction and wind-adjusted VAPP
Runways: departure defaults to the longest runway; SimBrief's arrival runway is kept when it exists in the database
Route: imported plans without a SimBrief distance now add SID/STAR and airway allowance to the great-circle distance
Weather: METARs refresh every 10 minutes, show their age, and the summary now shows present weather and the actual ceiling (e.g. LIGHT RAIN · OVERCAST 800 FT)

UI/UX: polished the dashboard layout, added subtle hover card effects, and implemented a cleaner dark mode styling
App Update: added auto-update notifications and rate button link
Donate: integrated a dedicated donate feature

title: Release v2.1.0
items: Flight model: introduced segmented Concorde mission profile (climb, accel, cruise-climb segments, descent) and rewired ETE/trip/endurance calculations to use it
Performance: takeoff/landing runway requirements now apply METAR/elevation corrections (QNH, ISA delta, headwind/tailwind, runway elevation) with pressure/temperature/wind breakdown in UI
Ops safety: added Operational Alerts for fuel endurance deficit, alternate risk, MTOW/MLW exceedance, runway shortfall, and notable tailwind conditions
Fuel logic: endurance now uses dynamic burn rate from mission profile, airborne fuel basis, and reserve timing for more realistic pass/fail checks
Fuel display: alternate fuel now reflects computed block alternate fuel instead of a simplified fixed-rate proxy
SimBrief flow: after import, app now prefers live METAR fetch (AviationWeather with fallback) and only keeps SimBrief METAR when live fetch is unavailable
UI copy: renamed usage counter label from SITE VISITS to EFB Launches
Desktop app: enabled external link opening via Tauri opener plugin and opener capability permission
Release metadata: version bumped globally to v2.1.0 across app, npm, Cargo, and Tauri config
UI cleanup: removed build marker display so the app surface shows semantic version only
